note: Workflows a `workflow_run` consumer deliberately does NOT watch (issue #349). `make check-workflows` fails when a workflow's completion is routed nowhere and no entry here records why — an omission has to be a dated decision, not an accident. An entry is refused without a `reason` and reported STALE once it names no workflow (the workflow was renamed or deleted), so this file cannot rot either.

security-scan \u2014 the daily vulnerabi.reason: Its red is already a work item with an owner: the scan's `fail_on` gate (critical/high WITH a fix, `data/security-policy.json`) is deliberate (`docs/SCANS.md`), `make security-issues` files the advisory issues, and `security-bot` turns one of them into a green PR. The reactor's Route B would file a SECOND issue per push to `main` (its marker carries the head sha), spending the issue-bot's 3-a-day budget on the same advisories.

run-failure-reactor \u2014 routes a fail.reason: It skips its own completion so a self-trigger loop is impossible (#286); listing itself is refused by the `workflow-run-self` rule. Its own red is what `code-review-bot` and `queued-alarm` report, and a red reactor run cannot route itself.

ci-hf-live \u2014 the merge-to-main real.reason: Its red is a named work item of its own class, not an implementation defect the reactor's Route B should re-file: the liveness gate (scripts/check_model_links_liveness.py LIVE=1 LIMIT=25) fails with the exact dead URL it probes, and the @pytest.mark.network live-set failures are real-Hub flakes to investigate. A main-merge or nightly red here IS the merge-time control itself, so routing every routine live-Hub blip to the issue-bot would duplicate the gate and spend the fix budget on the very flakes a probe pipeline exists to surface. A proven, persistent flake becomes a later dated revision, not the default — the security-scan precedent (#349).
